## Right now

Still in review from earlier sessions: the region music playtest, the restyled zombie art and the portrait popup, the four LL-029/030/031-era fixes, the stage-1-1 curve read-out and the rung price decision.

## Log (newest first)

- **2026-10-12** Cline — Fixed the in-water crash my own optional arguments caused. obj_mon/Draw_0 calls draw_self_part(0,0,1,0.75,0) - five arguments - while draw_self_part declares seven (argument0..argument6), and the optional _sx/_sy were being detected with `(argument_count > 5) ? argument5 : image_xscale`. The argument list is sized to the DECLARED arity and the unpassed parameters are padded with undefined, so argument_count was not 5, the ternary took the argument5 branch, and the next line multiplied by undefined: `undefined value at gml_Script_draw_self_part (line 33) - _x = x - sprite_get_xoffset(sprite_index)*_sx`, every frame a monster was in water. The error text itself proves the mechanism - 'undefined value' (arithmetic on undefined, so the slot EXISTS) rather than 'not set before reading it' - and image_xscale cannot be the culprit because obj_mon only ever assigns it real numbers (0, +/-abs, base_scale * _t, +/-base_scale, with base_scale 1 from Create or 0.25/0.5 from scr_level_spawn). scr_meta_log(_tag) declares one parameter and its loop prints all ten arguments, so argument_count = max(declared, passed) fits both cases; every other argument_count user in the project declares ZERO parameters, which is exactly why nothing else ever broke. The test is now is_undefined(argument5)/is_undefined(argument6) - the project's own 'not there' question, and independent of how argument_count is computed - with the defaults unchanged (image_xscale carries the monster's size AND sign, as the original sprite_xoffset code assumed). scr_drawGlowOutline carried the same brittle shape (argument_count > 0) and was fixed with it. obj_mon/Draw_0 keeps its short call on purpose: it is the test of the default path. Written up as LL-035. (fix-tower-click-mask) (`fix-tower-click-mask`)
- **2026-10-11** Cline — Fixed the silence on every stage, and it was not the music. rayu's runtime log (`GameMakerStudio2/debug.log`) had one line: `META  [MUSIC] region 1 "Wilted Sprouts" has no track yet - playing nothing` - the right region and the right title, so the table and music_for_region() were fine and only `_music.sound` was rejected. The guard at the top of scr_music_start_level tested it with `!is_real(_sound) \|\| _sound < 0`, and is_real() asks 'is this a plain number' while an asset reference is not one - so is_real(mus_world1) is false for a perfectly good sound and the guard refused EVERY region theme. The menu theme survived because obj_title and the Menu reach audio_play_sound_on() without passing through the guard. The guard now tests the two values music_data actually documents (-1 for 'not generated yet', undefined for 'no row') and the refusal says WHICH fired, the play line prints typeof(_sound) so the representation is on the record rather than assumed, and the loop-point pair 0.0/0.0 is no longer set for a whole-track loop (loop = true already repeats the track, and 0.0/0.0 depends on the runtime reading 'loop end 0' as 'end of file'). The asset was cleared on the way: mus_world1.yy is byte-identical to mus_world2.yy apart from the duration, and the IDE's asset cache held a valid converted mus_world1.wav with <Duration>163.53</Duration> beside it. Written up as LL-034, with the guard rail 'never ask a TYPE question about an asset'. (audio-region-music) (`audio-region-music`)
- **2026-10-11** Cline — Made the placement ghost ask the GRID instead of a collision mask. obj_tower_edit/Step_0 decided whether the cell under the ghost was taken with position_meeting(x, y, obj_tower), which reads the tower's 32x64 click mask - so the cell ABOVE a tower went red, while obj_tower/Create_0 blocks exactly one cell of LEVEL.path_grid and two towers are allowed to stack. It now asks the grid it is about to write into - mp_grid_get_cell(LEVEL.path_grid, (x + cell_w) div cell_w, (y + cell_h) div cell_h) != 0 - which is the same arithmetic obj_tower/Create_0 and scr_grid_block_instances use, plus the _spawn test that was already there (the spawn is not in the grid at all, and _spawn is also the parent of obj_wall, whose 32x32 art covers one cell, which backstops the part of the deploy countdown before scr_resetDrawPath puts the walls into the grid). The refusal now names its reason - META [PATH] placement refused: <why> - where it used to click, thud and vanish in silence, so a wrong-looking cell is one log line rather than a hunt. Folded into LL-033, whose mask caused both the tiny click area and the lying ghost. (fix-tower-click-mask) (`fix-tower-click-mask`)
- **2026-10-11** Cline — Split the tower art's size away from image_xscale, because a collision mask scales with image_xscale and the tower's click mask therefore arrived at half size. obj_tower already carried spr_tower_click_region (32x64: one cell wide, two cells tall) and it was correct; obj_tower/Create_0 drew the art with image_xscale = image_yscale = 0.5, so the mask was handed to the game as 16x32. The size moved into a new draw_scale (0.5 placed, 0.25 for the placement ghost), image_xscale/image_yscale are now +/-1 FACING ONLY, and a new scr_draw_self_scaled() is the one place that draws at the art's size and re-applies the facing sign. Every consumer of the size followed: scr_drawLight's shadow silhouette (guarded on the instance having a draw_scale, so monsters are unchanged), scr_drawGlowOutline (the halo now takes the size), draw_self_part (optional _sx/_sy, so its existing callers behave identically) and the upgrade tween, which now writes draw_scale and can no longer un-mirror a tower. The step-1 click box was deleted: Step_1 asks the mask itself with position_meeting, and _levelControl tie-breaks two stacked towers by the one whose own cell holds the pointer. In the same session all seven music tracks were mapped to their regions in music_data - mus_title plus mus_world1..mus_world6 - with the mapping read off each file's estimated tempo rather than assumed, and the brief's wiring table corrected: mus_world3 and mus_world4 are Desert and Jungle, not retired. Written up as LL-033. (fix-tower-click-mask) (`fix-tower-click-mask`)
- **2026-10-11** Cline — Chased the report that with no towers the zombies vanish a few seconds into every wave, the lives counter never moves and the wave still rewards the player. One mechanism could do it: the anti-softlock valve in scr_level_wait fired on ELAPSED TIME (6 s after the wave finished spawning) and destroyed EVERY live monster. A stopwatch cannot tell a monster that is walking from one that is stuck, and scr_zomb_pathSpeed puts a zombie at about 0.75 px/step (path_start passes an absolute speed) so it needs 20-45 s to cross a stage - the valve was not a net under the wave, it was the end of the wave. Because the monsters were deleted mid-route, the two arrival tests in scr_zomb_updatePosition never ran, lose_life() never fired, level_leaked stayed 0, Untouched was still earned and scr_level_clear paid seeds and clovers: the leak -> life -> game over mechanic was being discarded silently, and the leak path printed nothing at all, which is why it read as a missing mechanic rather than a bug. The valve now fires on evidence about the monster and only for that monster: scr_zomb_updatePosition counts steps in which path_position does not change (the path follower own progress report, which - unlike x/y - cannot be fooled by an instance that has lost its path and is drifting, LL-025), and scr_level_wait clears a monster that has not advanced for 5 s, logging path_free and path_retry and setting level_forced. Five seconds sits above the ~2 s obj_mon/Alarm_0 needs to escalate to the tower-ignoring escape grid, and a ten-minute per-wave latch (>= plus a one-shot flag, never ==, LL-029) keeps roadmap 4.4.1 promise that a stage can never hang. Every fate is now labelled exactly once in the log - kill / leak / valve - plus one line per monster giving path length, px/step and the projected walk time, so future thresholds are derived from the log rather than guessed. Written up as LL-031 and documented in systems_overview 4.3.1. (`fix-wave-valve`)
- **2026-10-11** Cline — Chased the request that towers mirror to face their target. obj_tower/Step_0 now calls the new scr_tower_faceTarget(target) once per step, after scr_runState has refreshed target, and mirrors with the idiom image_xscale = -abs(image_xscale) / abs(image_xscale) that scr_zomb_updatePosition already uses for monsters (LL-012). The helper handles every shape target takes - instance_nearest gives an instance or noone, find_all_range gives an array or the integer -1 - faces the NEAREST valid one, holds the last facing when there is nothing to face, and ignores a target within 2px of the tower so a monster in the cell directly above or below cannot strobe the sprite; it writes and logs only on a turn. Two latent traps surfaced with the flip: the upgrade tween wrote a bare positive image_xscale (which un-mirrored the tower on upgrade) and image_yscale = image_xscale (which becomes NEGATIVE once the scale can be negative, drawing the tower upside-down) - both fixed, magnitudes unchanged. scr_drawLight builds the shadow silhouette from sprite_width/sprite_xoffset and ignored image_xscale, so it mirrors now too, which also corrects left-walking zombie shadows. LL-012 extended with the three ways a flip dies. (`fix-tower-facing`)
- **2026-10-11** Cline — Chased the report that the Daisy Pusher plays its idle and return animations about three times too fast after its sprite was swapped for the 5-frame spr_daisy_*_192x trio. Two of the three tower states set image_speed - a SPEED - where a duration was meant: the idle loop was 0.25 and the return was 1, so the period scaled with the frame count (15 frames at 0.25 is 60 steps; 5 frames at 0.25 is 20). The attack was already frame-count independent because it divided by frame_number, which is exactly why the bug looked like bad art. Fixed by asking for a PERIOD everywhere: new scr_animSpeedForSteps(sprite, steps) returns the image_speed that plays a sprite through once in N steps whatever its frame count, and normalises the sprite's declared speed type (image_speed is a multiplier, not frames-per-step); new scr_tower_animSpeed(slot, steps) is the ONE place a tower's speed is set, and logs the period once per animation per tower; the durations live as anim_seconds on obj_tower (1.00s idle / 0.25s return = the periods the old 15-frame trio played at); sprite_list is now indexed by a new TOWER_ANIM enum instead of 0/1/2 literals; and the return state exits on state_time >= anim_steps rather than on image_index, which fired up to a frame early at a fractional speed. obj_tower_edit's placement ghost no longer relies on image_single (a GM8 variable that does not exist in GMS2) and holds frame 0. Written up as LL-030. (`fix-tower-anim-speed`)
- **2026-10-10** Cline — Chased the playtest report that some towers stick in the attack animation. scr_tower_shoot left the attack state only on `state_time == frame_number`, but frame_number = room_speed/data[TOWER.fire_rate] is a FLOAT once fire_rate is scaled - the level ladder multiplies it by 1.04/1.08/... (tower_levels.gml) and placement folds in the garden floor and clover bonuses - so a base 3/s tower is 19.23 frames at L2. state_time is an integer, so that equality could never hold and the tower looped the attack sprite forever (and stopped dealing damage). Fixed: the state exits on >= frame_number, damage and particles fire once via did_damage/did_particles flags with clamped frames, and the target list is re-validated every frame so a target that dies or leaves range mid-swing returns the tower to idle. Written up as LL-029. (`fix-tower-attack-stuck`)
- **2026-10-06** Rayu — Playtest validation: 'Plants block one 32x32 grid cell, not a 2x2' - the pathing works as of the last test. The reloaded build also ran without the Input dispatch crash, so the saved-key_type fixes hold. That closes fix-tower-cell-footprint, fix-zombie-north-drift, fix-keytype-dispatch, fix-saved-keytype, run-script-dispatch and gm-reload-verify; the validated build is committed (e924703). (`fix-tower-cell-footprint`)
- **2026-10-06** Cline — Chased the Input crash that appeared after the run_script migration: 'Variable obj_spawn.time_keeper not set before reading it' from scr_drawSwitchTimer, called by Input/Step_0 -> run_script. Decoding the save file showed [KeyInputData] 1 still holds the listeners as type-marker-15 values (100417/100415), i.e. ds_list_write/read DOES round-trip a function reference - it comes back as a value that is STILL CALLABLE, so scr_load_keys' is_callable() guard passed and key_type was replaced by the stale array; the dispatch then ran whatever script the old handle now indexes (scr_drawTimerExt for LL-026, scr_drawSwitchTimer once run_script added a script). run_script()'s guard cannot see it: the value is not undefined, not a number and not non-callable. Fix: scr_load_keys/scr_load_gamepad no longer read slot 1, and scr_save_keys/scr_save_gamepad blank it so an older build cannot read it either; the live save file was purged too. Written up as LL-028, which corrects LL-026's premise that the value comes back as a plain number. (`fix-saved-keytype`)
- **2026-10-06** Cline — Replaced every script_execute() in the project (14 call sites across 12 files) with a new run_script(script_name, target=noone, arguments_list=[]). It returns undefined unless the name passes !is_undefined() && is_callable(); when target != noone and instance_exists(target) it re-binds with method(target, script_name) so the call runs in that instance's scope, otherwise it runs in the caller's scope as script_execute() did. GML has no argument spread, so arguments_list is forwarded through a switch on array_length (0..4 - the widest site, for_grid, passes 4) and a longer list logs via scr_meta_log instead of failing silently. Sites: Input/Step_0 (the LL-026 dispatch), scr_runState, scr_stpButton, scr_updateReciever, the for_* iterators, and _oTextInput Create/Step/Draw. run_script is not a GameMaker built-in (LL-005 checked); LL-026's guard rails now point at it. (`run-script-dispatch`)
- **2026-10-06** Cline — Pathfinding was still wrong after LL-025. mp_grid_add_rectangle and mp_grid_add_instances floor BOTH edges and iterate INCLUSIVELY, so the tower's x+-cell_w/2 rectangle - whose far edge lands exactly on the next cell boundary - marked a 2x2 block instead of the one 32x32 cell it occupies (and any instance whose bbox far edge hit a boundary over-blocked the same way, which is how the walled pen's one-cell exit could seal). Fixed: obj_tower Create/Destroy block and clear exactly one cell by index (grid_col/grid_row); obj_tower_edit blocks one cell for the candidate and one per existing blocker; a new scr_grid_block_instances() replaces mp_grid_add_instances over the live grid in scr_resetDrawPath and obj_mon/Alarm_0. Written up as LL-027. (`fix-tower-cell-footprint`)
- **2026-10-06** Cline — Fixed the Input._objSwitch crash. key_type holds function references, but scr_save_keys persisted it through ds_list_write, which cannot represent a function - so on the next launch key_type came back as numbers and Input/Step_0's script_execute() ran whatever script that number indexed (scr_drawTimerExt, which reads the unrecovered _objSwitch). scr_save_keys no longer saves key_type, scr_load_keys rejects a non-callable loaded key_type and keeps the freshly built one, Input/Step_0 only script_execute()s a callable, and scr_drawTimerExt resolves _objSwitch with asset_get_index and bails when absent. Written up as LL-026. (`fix-keytype-dispatch`)
- **2026-10-06** Cline — Zombies marched north through the walls. obj_mon/Draw_72 (Pre Draw) and Draw_73 (Post Draw) both subtracted z_climb*2-12 - a draw-only offset applied twice - and Alarm_0 threw the live path away (path_end + path_clear_points) before asking the grid for a new one, so one failed re-path left the monster with no path and nothing rewriting its y. Draw_73 now restores the offset, and scr_path_replace() probes a scratch path and only commits on success, so the last valid path is kept. Also made the tower's grid block and its clear the same rectangle. Written up as LL-025. (`fix-zombie-north-drift`)
- **2026-10-06** Cline — Closed the 'commit the curve work' card: every file it said was untracked is already committed in HEAD and git status is clean, so the card had gone stale. Noted the LL-024 lesson (a call to an undefined function reports as a variable read in the CALLER's scope). (`git-commit-curve`)

Both now live in tower_levels.gml beside tower_rung_cost(). (`fix-tower-upgrade-crash`)
